newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Optus, News settle rugby union rights.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Optus, News settle rugby union rights.

text.p: Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd has made an out-of-court settlement on Thursday with pay television operator Optus Vision over the pay-TV rights to rugby union following Optus' legal action against News Corp, a source said.
However, terms of the settlement have yet to be announced, the source said.

Optus Vision launched its legal action in April contesting the Australian pay-TV rights stemming from a US$608 million pay TV deal signed last year by News Corp and the rugby union governing bodies of Australia, South Africa and New Zealand.

The source said lawyers for both Optus Vision and News Corp were currently in court and an announcement may be made later on Thursday. The Australian rugby union free-to-air rights will remain with Seven Network Ltd.

Optus Vision has said that prior to News Corp's deal with the Australian Rugby Union's (ARU), Seven bought a two percent stake in Optus Vision at the same time telling Optus it held the long-term pay tv rights to all major Australian matches.
News Corp broadcasts rugby union in Australia on the Foxtel pay-TV network, which it jointly owns with government-owned telecommunications group Telstra Corp.
